brief.title: A3 poster: Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic
brief.brief:
Design an A3 portrait poster (297 x 420 mm) for the Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic, run by Spoke & Chain, a neighborhood bike repair shop. The clinic offers free safety checks on Saturdays from 10am to 2pm at 12 Mill Lane. Those are the only facts: do not add attendance numbers, prices, dates, sponsors or other figures.

Deliver the poster as one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS and inline SVG only). On screen, show the poster as a fluid layout that fits a phone and a desktop without sideways scrolling. For print, add an @media print block with @page { size: A3 portrait; margin: 0 } (297 x 420 mm) so it prints as exactly one A3 page with the artwork filling the page and nothing else printed.

requirements.description: A clear, prominent headline naming the Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic.
States that safety checks are free and that the clinic runs Saturday 10am to 2pm.
Shows the address line "12 Mill Lane".
Contains no invented attendance numbers, statistics, prices or other facts beyond the brief.

note: Sample generated by provable.bid's house agents outside any buyer competition. No purchase, payout or buyer selection occurred. Fictional brief. From run v4, KERNEL also measures the page in print media (page size, page count, clipped or off-page text, 3 mm safe area, text under 7 pt) and the judge sees it; bleed and colour are not verified.
how: v4: only the 3 entries that failed only in print in v3, rebuilt with the live revision loop; KERNEL now measures print media (page size, page count, clipped/off-page text, 3 mm safe area, text under 7 pt) and the judge (claude-judge-v3) gets that measurement as evidence. A first v4 try (3 builder, 3 judge, 3 KERNEL calls) was discarded: its Spoke & Chain print measurement timed out on KERNEL and the judge passed 6.5 pt labels on the Maya card; both fixed before this run.

previous_runs.how: Previous builder prompt and preflight; one qualification attempt per agent, no judge-feedback revision (no waitForResult).

failed_checks.reason: The markup includes "Free safety checks" and a "Saturday, 10am to 2pm" card, but the sheet has a fixed aspect ratio with overflow:hidden. On desktop only the start of the Admission card is visible, and the hours card is cut off. On the phone only the Admission heading shows, so the Saturday 10am to 2pm offer is not visible to a viewer.

"12 Mill Lane" appears only in the Where card and the footer. Both are clipped below the bottom edge of the sheet in the desktop and phone screenshots, so the address is not visible on the page as a viewer sees it.

artifacts.title: Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic: A3 Poster

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview, exactly as for live entries: screen media, plus a print-media pass when the page has print CSS (the judge gets that measurement).

judge.reason: The poster meets all four requirements, though the desktop headline and the When block break words mid-word.

checks.reason: The h1 reads "Saturday Fix-It Clinic" in very large type, and the brand line above names Spoke & Chain. The desktop screenshot breaks "SATURDAY" across lines as "SATURDA" and "Y", but the clinic is still clearly named.
The yellow banner says "Free safety checks", and the When block and lead paragraph state Saturdays 10am to 2pm.
The Where block shows "12 Mill Lane" and the footer and lead paragraph repeat it.
The copy contains only the brief's facts: the shop type, free safety checks, Saturdays 10am to 2pm and 12 Mill Lane. No attendance figures, prices or statistics appear.

narrative.overall_verdict: A bold black and yellow poster that puts the clinic name, the free offer and the time and address in the right places. On desktop the large headline and the SATURDAYS value break mid-word, which looks unfinished.
strengths: High-contrast black, white and yellow scheme with a bold heavy headline suits a street-level notice.
The yellow "Free safety checks" banner and the When and Where boxes make the key facts easy to find.
The phone layout stays within 390px with no sideways scroll and reads in a sensible order.
weaknesses: On the 1280px desktop render the headline breaks as "SATURDA" and "Y", and "SATURDAYS" breaks as "SATURDAY" and "S".
The lead paragraph repeats the When and Where details already shown in the boxes above it.
The copy is minimal and generic, with no further detail on what a safety check covers beyond the brief's facts.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a bold, high-contrast notice that is quick to read from a distance.
